title: Kaspersky: Pakistan faced more than 9.4 million cyberattacks in a year, backdoor attacks up 50%
date_note: Publication day of the PhoneWorld and Profit articles; neither gives the date of the Islamabad summit talk.
summary: PhoneWorld reports that Kaspersky said Pakistan faced more than 9.4 million cyberattacks between November 2025 and October 2026, figures given by a Kaspersky researcher at the Cyber Threat Intelligence Summit 2026 in Islamabad. Backdoor attacks increased by 50%, with more than 233,000 detections, and Kaspersky detected more than 3.1 million web-based attacks. Kaspersky says it tracked seven APT actors targeting Pakistan, including Mirage Kitten and SideWinder.
plain: Kaspersky says its products saw more than 9.4 million cyberattacks in Pakistan over a year, with attacks that plant hidden backdoors up 50%.
exec: Vendor telemetry points to rising backdoor activity and active espionage groups aimed at Pakistan.
action: Kaspersky, as reported by PhoneWorld, advises continuous network monitoring, faster incident response, employee training and clear rules that keep confidential data out of external AI tools.

evidence.quote: Pakistan faced more than 9.4 million cyberattacks between November 2025 and October 2026
backdoor attacks increased by 50%, with more than 233,000 detections
detected more than 3.1 million web-based attacks in Pakistan during the same period

validation.note: PhoneWorld and Profit by Pakistan Today both relay the same Kaspersky figures; Kaspersky's own release was not read, so the figures rest on Kaspersky alone. Business Recorder answered 403. Profit gives the period only as the past 12 months.
